Twenty-nine comments

Within a Mile of Dublin

I found this gem in Breathnach’s Ceol Rince Na hEireann, Volume 2 (# 179). It goes wonderfully as a slow, swingy, slippery set up to a fast, driving reel (such as Last Night’s Fun).

↳ Posted by Will Harmon on June 7th, 2001.

Within a Mile of Dublin

I learnt this tune a few years ago from a recording by Barney McKenna. He plays it first a couple of times as it is notated here, then with F naturals instead of F sharps, then switches back to major again to finish with. The change of mood (not to mention his playing) makes it a very nice set indeed. I also sometimes like to follow it with something in Em, like Cooley’s.

↳ Posted by dolefulshades on June 17th, 2001.

On Na Connerys Part II, they play a slightly different setting of this tune following the Bobby Casey’s that I posted -- it’s a current favorite set!

Zina

↳ Posted by Zina Lee on September 8th, 2001.

Just an experiment, as a strathspey

Found myself playing this as a strathspey on fiddle once. I like it better shifted down a string to Gmix, but I suppose I should notate it in Dmix for the sake of consistency. Meant to be played fast, as in the Cape Breton tradition.
